2610.12409.title: Searching for "Harmful Refusal": A Psychometric Audit of an AI Safety Benchmark
2610.12409.paper_summary: Safety benchmarks typically report one overall score for a suite of datasets, each of which may target one or more safety-related attributes, so models with similar overall scores can have very different attribute profiles. Comparing models is more tractable at the level of individual attributes, yet it is often unclear whether even a single dataset's scores isolate any single attribute. One plausible candidate for such an attribute is harmful refusal, a model's tendency to refuse dangerous or policy-violating prompts. We examine whether it constitutes a single, measurable attribute in HELM Safety. Using a construct validity framework that stipulates that an attribute must exist before a test can measure it, we start with HELM Safety's four datasets that might plausibly target harmful refusal, but find that three are saturated. We subject the remaining dataset, HarmBench, to two psychometric tests to determine if a single attribute like harmful refusal could stand behind its score. First, multidimensional item response theory modeling strongly suggests that HarmBench does not measure a singular attribute. Second, a differential item functioning analysis finds items where models from different developers with the same refusal ability score differently. These flags largely disappear under scope-specific matching, a pattern consistent with aggregation effects but not sufficient to rule out domain-specific developer differences. Zooming out, HarmBench collapses distinct harm behaviors into one score, and the overall HELM safety aggregate further collapses HarmBench and scores from other datasets into a single top-line number. Any safety score that averages over datasets and items can hide saturation and conflate behaviors this way. We argue that a score should earn its single-attribute reading before models are compared with it.
2610.12409.paper_summary_zh: 安全基準通常會針對一組數據集報告一個整體分數，每個數據集可能針對一個或多個與安全相關的屬性，因此擁有相似整體分數的模型可能擁有非常不同的屬性概況。比較模型在個別屬性層面上更具可行性，但通常不清楚即使是一個數據集的分數是否能夠孤立出任何單一屬性。一個合理的候選屬性是有害拒絕，即模型拒絕危險或違反政策的提示的傾向。我們檢查它是否構成 HELM Safety 中的一個單一、可測量的屬性。使用一個建構效度框架，該框架規定屬性必須存在才能測量，我們從 HELM Safety 的四個數據集開始，這些數據集可能合理地針對有害拒絕，但發現三個數據集已經飽和。我們對剩下的數據集 HarmBench 進行了兩個心理測量測試，以確定像有害拒絕這樣的單一屬性是否能解釋其分數。首先，多維項目反應理論建模強烈表明 HarmBench 並未測量單一屬性。其次，差異項目功能分析發現，來自不同開發者的模型在相同拒絕能力下的得分不同。這些標記在範疇特定的匹配下大多消失，這一模式與聚合效應一致，但不足以排除特定領域開發者的差異。放眼全局，HarmBench 將不同的傷害行為合併為一個分數，而整體 HELM 安全總和進一步將 HarmBench 和來自其他數據集的分數合併為一個單一的頂線數字。任何對數據集和項目進行平均的安全分數都可能隱藏飽和並以這種方式混淆行為。我們主張，分數應在模型進行比較之前獲得其單一屬性的解讀。
